name: Evil-merodach
overview: Evil-merodach was a male king of Babylon mentioned in the Bible. His primary identification is as the ruler of Babylon, as noted in 2 Kings 25:27. There is no additional tribal or familial information provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The name Evil-merodach means 'worshiper of Marduk[s]' or is corrupted to read as 'fool of blessing,' reflecting its Babylonian origin. His title, King of Babylon, simply denotes his royal position over the city of Babel as recorded in 2 Kings 25:27.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Evil-merodach beyond his role as King of Babylon. No relatives or descendants are mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Evil-merodach's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his kingship of Babylon during a pivotal period. His mention in 2 Kings 25:27 places him historically after the fall of Jerusalem, marking him as a figure in the aftermath of Judah's exile. Though details are sparse, his reign represents a transitional moment in the history of Babylonian dominance over the Israelites.
